comparator.institution: Wageningen University & Research / Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: BBNDD current handbook:120SLU+6strategic planning+18thesis=144common;12SocietyandPolicy restricted;24adviser-consultedopen=180. Neutral official-order route retained. SLU students only; WUR courses are the third-year exchange, not a programme open to ordinary WUR students. Before thesis complete102prescribedcredits includingall60B1; all120SLUcredits may precede thesis. Complete zeroEC safety before applicable activities. Partner syllabus establishes course-specific entry and compulsory fieldwork. WURBBNDD controls recognition and180structure; ordinarySLUdegree tables are not added on top.

components.name: Forest Management Methods
components.note: Requires 15 prior credits in forestry, biology, landscape architecture or another listed relevant field; the first-year studies satisfy this requirement.

components.name: Vegetation Design
components.note: Requires 7.5 prior credits each in forestry science and landscape architecture, supplied by the first-year curriculum.

components.name: Forest and Landscape Governance
components.note: Requires 7.5 prior landscape-architecture credits, supplied by Analysis of Forested Landscapes.

components.name: Business Management in Forest and Landscape
Forest and Landscape Biodiversity Conservation and Ecosystem Services
Strategic Planning in Forest and Nature Conservation
components.note: Integrative strategic conservation planning includes a compulsory field practical. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety are additional zero-credit requirements; complete relevant safety training before activities. The current strategic-planning course specifies a €120 student contribution.

components.name: BSc Thesis Forest and Nature Conservation (Double Degree SLU)
components.note: Required 18-credit individual scientific research project for participating SLU double-degree students. Complete at least 102 prescribed credits, including all first-year credits, before starting. A proposal, research, report and presentation are required.

components.name: Human Geography: Theory and Practice
components.note: First listed six-credit Society and Policy option selected.

components.name: Communicating for Sustainability and Responsible Innovation
components.note: Second listed six-credit Society and Policy option selected. Prior environmental-policy knowledge is assumed.

components.name: Open elective space
components.note: Twenty-four credits of elective study, chosen in consultation with the study adviser, complete this 180-credit example.

questionsApplications.label: How can forest biodiversity, landscapes and ecosystems be conserved and managed under climate change?
How can ecological and social evidence be combined in forest and landscape decisions?
How should conflicts over land, livelihoods and ecosystem services be governed?

alternatives.concept: Combine biodiversity, ecological processes and environmental systems with law, economics, institutions and social-environmental research to examine conservation decisions. Water, climate and land-use pressures connect environmental evidence with public action. Dedicated tree and forest-management training remains a difference.

alternatives.labelRationale: Replaces weak human-biomedical selections with concrete soil, geospatial, environmental chemistry and resource-impact investigation while retaining biodiversity and ecosystem processes.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Eight courses unique against the closest programme prioritise ecological/soil/spatial/physical investigation and resource-impact methods over its sustained legal/social/political strand.

alternatives.concept: Examine environmental governance through law, public economics, political institutions, justice and communication. Empirical research, data and causal analysis inform policy evaluation, while water, soils, resource pressures and remediation supply an environmental foundation. The priority is social-environmental decisions rather than a full ecology or forestry sequence.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The double-degree target offers two equally formal 12-EC WUR specialisations, Society and Policy and Ecology and Conservation. Neither is clearly broader or less specialised, so the first current-handbook specialisation is selected before considering UCR fit.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Current workbook offerings and earlier formal prerequisites verified for all24courses. PPD is in Year1; 6advanced courses. Core ecology precedes advanced marine/farming study where selected; mathematical, legal, laboratory and economic-method prerequisites are earlier. Open-curriculum advisory progression does not add formal gates.

basisLabels: Spatial, climate, quantitative and environmental evidence for landscape decisions

basisLabels: Human–nature relations, livelihoods, economics, policy and forest-landscape governance

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest ecological/social environmental response, followed by ecological investigation and then environmental institutions/evidence, implements the exact target interests. Changes in priority produce8/10/11unique-course pairwise differences. All three pass current feasibility; no fourth candidate. These are liberal-arts responses to the documented double-degree academic substance, not recreations of professional forestry, landscape design or two-country qualification arrangements.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Habitat fragmentation, extinction, conservation planning and species-protection projects directly address biodiversity conservation; forest ecosystem-service trade-offs are broader in the partner course.
Population, community and ecosystem dynamics and ecological modelling address an important core of forest ecology; UCR covers ecosystems more broadly.
GIS databases, georeferencing, spatial-data processing and environmental analysis directly implement this spatial method; forestry datasets and scope differ.
No selected course supplies the tree anatomy, physiology, taxonomy and silviculture sequence.
No selected course combines the defining physical landscape analysis with sociocultural landscape use and experience. GIS alone does not reproduce the integrated course.
Silvicultural operations, forest rotation and owner-oriented management prescriptions remain specialist differences.
The forest-design project and experiential vegetation planning are not supplied by sustainable agriculture.
No selected course provides tree-damage collection, pest/pathogen diagnostics and forest-health management.
Actors, power, institutions, participation and environmental policy evaluation directly address forest-landscape governance methods; applications are broader at UCR.
Environmental communication, contested public texts and public engagement form a meaningful part of sustainability communication; WUR also requires focus-group research not reproduced here.
General economics does not supply the integrated financial statements, forest-investment appraisal and organisational management.
EU political institutions are not a strategic protected-area action-plan and field-practical course.
General law and justice is not sustained human-geography theory and research.
The compulsory18-credit thesis differs from scheduled UCR courses. Optional UCR research is shown separately, outside180credits.
Genuine open choice remains explicit; do not invent a course counterpart.

notes.text: The WUR–SLU route combines two years of forest-and-landscape study at SLU with a Wageningen year, an 18-credit thesis and specialist fieldwork. The UCR options develop related ecological, environmental and governance interests, but do not reproduce the tree biology, silviculture, forest design, business and health sequence or the double-degree qualifications. Optional UCR research is additional to each 180-credit schedule.

audience.programmeDescription: This double-degree route connects SLU Forest and Landscape with Wageningen Forest and Nature Conservation. Students study forest ecology, trees, landscape analysis and design, management, business and governance, then complete the Wageningen requirements.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR programmes respond through ecological and social conservation questions, environmental investigation, or policy and institutions. Specialist forestry and landscape design, structured fieldwork, the required 18-credit thesis and the two-country degree arrangement remain important differences.
